settings.name_in_paper: Best fair intervention identification in a causal model under a budget constraint
unmapped: Arms are K known soft interventions P_k(V|pa(V)) on a node V of a causal DAG; learner knows these conditionals and P(X|pa(X)) for children of the binary sensitive attribute S, enabling importance-sampling information leakage between arms
Goal: identify the best arm among E-fair arms, where fairness is a counterfactual constraint |zeta_k^{s',s}|, |zeta_k^{s,s'}| < E
Average sampling cost constraint with per-arm costs c_k, a_k, b_k and budget B; learner may also sample with chosen sensitive attribute (hard intervention on S)
Learner observes S, V, pa(V), children of S and their parents, and Y after each pull
Outcome Y implicitly bounded (used in concentration), range not stated explicitly
settings.definition_quote: The goal is to find a soft intervention on a given node to maximize the outcome while meeting a fairness constraint by counterfactual estimation with only partial knowledge of the causal model. ... we restrict our theoretical analysis to bounding the error probability of the problem defined as $e(B) = \mathbb{P}(\hat{k}(B)\neq k^\star)$. Here $k^\star$ is the best fair intervention

algorithms.name: Constraint Successive Rejection (CSR)
requires_knowledge_of: conditionals P(X|pa(X)) for children of S

symbols.rho_star: problem-dependent constant max{log(20/Delta), log(12/Delta^{s'}), log(12/Delta^s)} from outcome and fairness gaps
symbols.H_bar: hardness max_{k != k*} rho_k^3 / (2^{-2 rho_k} v*(B,R*(k))^2)
symbols.logbar_nT: harmonic number sum_{i=1}^{n(T)} 1/i with n(T) = ceil(log2 log10 sqrt(T))

conditions: a best fair arm k* exists with |xi_{k*}^{s,s'}|, |xi_{k*}^{s',s}| < E

source.quote: Consider a problem instance with $K$ candidate arms. Suppose $K>1$ and there exists a best fair arm $k^*$ satisfying $\abs{\xi_{k^*}^{s,s'}},\abs{\xi_{k^*}^{s',s}} < \mathcal{E}$. ... The error probability of Algorithm 1 is bounded as e(T,B) \leq 8K^2\rho^\star\exp(-\frac{T}{8\bar{H}\overline{\log}(n(T))})

results.notes: Restated in appendix as Theorem 10. Probability field set to expectation as it bounds a probability (not a high-probability statement); problem constants depend on budget LP value v*.

symbols.n_T: number of phases n(T) = ceil(log2 log10 sqrt(T))
symbols.xi_star: min over arms of distance of |xi_k| to fairness threshold E
symbols.v_star: v*(B) = min over nonempty arm subsets R of the budget-allocation LP value v*(B,R)

conditions: no fair arm exists: for all k, |xi_k^{s,s'}| >= E or |xi_k^{s',s}| >= E

source.quote: Suppose that $K > 1$ and for all arms $k\in [K]$ either $\abs*{\xi_k^{s,s'}} \geq \mathcal{E}$ or $\abs*{\xi_k^{s', s}} \geq \mathcal{E}$. ... Then, the probability that the algorithm declares no fair arm exists is at least $$1 - 4 K n(T)  \exp (-\frac{(\xi^*)^2 T }{32 n(T)^3 \overline{\log}\left(n(T)\right)}v^*(B)^2),$$

results.notes: Stated as lower bound on probability of correctly declaring no fair arm; recorded as upper bound on the failure probability (complement).
